name: IEEE754 Float Inspector
blurb: sign, exponent and mantissa bits of a float
intro: Shows how a decimal value is stored as an IEEE 754 half, bfloat16, float or double: the sign, exponent and fraction bits, the exact value stored, the rounding error and the spacing to the neighbours. Or give a bit pattern (0x…) to decode it.

inputs.label: Value or bits
inputs.help: Decimal (0.1, -1.5e-3), inf, nan, or a bit pattern like 0x3DCCCCCD.

examples.title: Decode a float read from a sensor register

usage: Give value as a decimal string (or inf / nan) or a hex bit pattern starting with 0x, and format = binary32 | binary64 | binary16 | bfloat16. Returns the bit pattern, sign, exponent field and unbiased exponent, significand, the exact stored decimal, the rounding error (absolute and relative), the ULP and next values, and the format's range. The result's bits object carries the sign/exponent/fraction bit strings. Use it to explain float precision, decode raw float registers or check a constant.
sources: IEEE 754-2019 Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic, sections 3.4 (binary interchange formats) and 4.3.1 (round to nearest, ties to even)
